## Purpose

Reclassify 18S OTU representative sequences against the **PR2 (Protist Ribosomal
Reference) database <https://pr2-database.org/> using mothur's Wang/RDP-style naive Bayesian
classifier. This replaces the default SILVA-based assignments produced by the
C-MAIKI pipeline. PR2 is curated specifically for eukaryotic SSU rRNA and
generally provides finer-resolution protistan taxonomy than SILVA for 18S data.

Inputs:

- `OTUs.97.rep.fasta` — representative sequences at 97% OTU clustering (C-MAIKI output)
- `pr2_version_5.1.1_SSU_mothur.fasta` — PR2 reference alignment
- `pr2_version_5.1.1_SSU_mothur.tax` — PR2 taxonomy strings

Output: a `.wang.taxonomy` file that can be read into phyloseq / dplyr in place
of the SILVA-derived taxonomy table.


```{bash paths, eval=FALSE}
# ---- Paths ----

# PR2 reference (where the gzipped files live, also where they unzip to)
PR2_DIR="/Users/becca/Documents/records/database_PR2"
PR2_FASTA="${PR2_DIR}/pr2_version_5.1.1_SSU_mothur.fasta"
PR2_TAX="${PR2_DIR}/pr2_version_5.1.1_SSU_mothur.tax"

# C-MAIKI OTU representative sequences (input)
REP_FASTA="/Users/becca/Documents/current projects/Manuscript Storm Wali/data/processed/s18_microbial/cmaiki_pipeline/OTUs.97.rep.fasta"

# Output directory for the reclassified taxonomy
OUT_DIR="/Users/becca/Documents/current projects/Manuscript Storm Wali/data/processed/s18_microbial/pr2_alignment"
mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}"

# mothur executable
MOTHUR="/Applications/mothur/mothur"


# ---- Step 1 — Decompress the PR2 reference files ----
# Safe to re-run: skips gunzip silently if the .gz is already gone.
[ -f "${PR2_FASTA}.gz" ] && gunzip "${PR2_FASTA}.gz"
[ -f "${PR2_TAX}.gz" ]   && gunzip "${PR2_TAX}.gz"

# Sanity check that both decompressed files exist
ls -lh "${PR2_FASTA}" "${PR2_TAX}"


# ---- Step 2 — Run the mothur classifier ----
# classify.seqs parameters:
#   reference   — PR2 reference alignment fasta
#   taxonomy    — PR2 taxonomy strings (must match the reference)
#   cutoff=80   — bootstrap confidence threshold (mothur default = 80)
#   probs=F     — strip the bootstrap brackets from the taxonomy strings
#   processors  — number of processors for mothur to use
"${MOTHUR}" "#set.logfile(name=${OUT_DIR}/pr2_classify.logfile);
              set.dir(output=${OUT_DIR});
              classify.seqs(fasta=${REP_FASTA},
                            reference=${PR2_FASTA},
                            taxonomy=${PR2_TAX},
                            cutoff=80,
                            probs=F,
                            processors=3)"
                            
                            rm mothur.1779804095.logfile
```

## Output files

Mothur writes three files into `${OUT_DIR}`. The naming uses the last segment
of the template fasta after the final dot, so v5.1.1 produces files prefixed
with `OTUs.97.rep.0_SSU_mothur.wang.*`:

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `OTUs.97.rep.0_SSU_mothur.wang.taxonomy` | OTU → full PR2 lineage (load this into phyloseq) |
| `OTUs.97.rep.0_SSU_mothur.wang.tax.summary` | Hierarchical count summary across the taxonomy tree |
| `OTUs.97.rep.0_SSU_mothur.wang.flip.accnos` | OTU IDs whose query sequence was reverse-complemented for a better hit |

The `.flip.accnos` file is informational — mothur already used the reversed
orientation for the classification. It just tells you which OTUs were
oriented opposite to PR2's reference convention.
